A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same critical-neuron identification study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original neuron-masking experiments across 21 models, downstream benchmark evaluations, localization comparisons and appendix robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component controls, neuron-subset experiments, precision comparisons and normalization diagnostics.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain Gaussian input perturbations, activation-difference sensitivity ranking and greedy neuron masking until the perplexity threshold is reached. The new component and normalization interventions are evaluation controls, not changes to the proposed identification algorithm.

E1.justification: WikiText-103, C4, the seven downstream benchmarks and the existing input-type, language and factual-question tests are retained. New experiments reuse this coverage with different component interventions or numerical settings. The revised MATH citation does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains the same evaluated localization alternatives: random selection, activation magnitude and gradient magnitude. Newly discussed super-weights, super-neurons and Wasserstein neurons are not added as evaluated baselines. Component-restricted masking supplies additional controls rather than a new competing localization method.

E3.justification: v2 introduces substantial controlled evaluation designs: fixed neuron sets across fp16/fp32/fp64, all nonempty subsets of two four-neuron sets, component-specific masking at 10/100/1000 neurons, and layerwise LayerNorm removal with RMSNorm and NaN/Inf diagnostics. Existing benchmark generation and scoring protocols remain unchanged. Tables 3 and 13 inconsistently describe identical component-control values.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and Appendices A.9–A.10 add tests of component specificity, cooperative necessity, numerical precision and normalization-related explanations for collapse. These substantially extend v1's threshold, input robustness, fine-tuning and activation-scaling analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports mean and standard deviation over 100 trials for random up_proj and attention masking in Tables 12 and 14, and discloses seed=42. Figure 3 still averages 10 random trials; the new reports do not establish increased runs for that experiment. Tables 13 and 15 promise standard deviations in their captions but omit them from the cells.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and matched appendix results are retained, while substantial new findings are reported. For example, v2 Table 5 gives Llama-3.2-1B perplexity of 1,585,570.7467 after masking all four critical neurons, versus at most 24.8507 for any proper nonempty subset. Tables 4 and 12–18 add precision, component, numerical-diagnostic and response results; these are additional experiments, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix A.10 introduces definitions of per-layer RMSNorm change and its average across layers in Equations 13–14. These are limited diagnostic definitions. The original optimization problem, sensitivity estimator, assumptions and complexity argument remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the central claims of ultra-sparse critical neuron sets, concentration in outer-layer MLP down_proj components and abrupt collective collapse across 21 models. Added controls support these retained claims rather than redefine their main scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific interpretations excluding numerical precision and LayerNorm instability as explanations, and proposes a possible connection to attention sinks in Appendix A.11. These refine the retained information-bottleneck and cooperative-circuit account. Defensive strategies remain future proposals rather than demonstrated solutions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and reproducibility statement, specifies seed=42, and discloses Claude 3 use for debugging in Appendix A.12. The original hardware, implementation framework, principal hyperparameters and benchmark generation details are retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's contents.

R1.justification: v2 replaces detailed neuroscience lesion-study framing with AI perturbation precedents, substantially expands its claimed distinctions from Yu et al.'s super-weights, and discusses super-neurons and Wasserstein neurons. Appendix A.11 also adds attention-sink and representation-learning connections. This materially revises research positioning beyond bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the neuroscience introduction, rewrites parts of related work, adds descriptive experiment subheadings and introduces ethics/reproducibility, acknowledgement and LLM-usage sections. Author order and publication headers change. Most existing methodology, evaluation and conclusion prose remains closely matched, so the language revision is targeted rather than comprehensive.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial tabular displays for component controls, precision comparisons, neuron subsets and normalization diagnostics. It reformats and relocates existing tables within a conference layout, including moving response examples closer to their discussion. Figures 1–7 retain their plotted content; Figure 1's expanded caption repeats probabilities already visible in v1.

improvement.justification: The subset and precision experiments provide useful validation missing from v1, particularly for cooperative collapse, and the code link improves reproducibility information. However, identical values receive conflicting masking descriptions in Tables 3 and 13, promised uncertainty is missing in Tables 13 and 15, and precision controls cover only three small models. These reporting and coverage limits temper the benefit, yielding a supported but limited overall improvement.
